In this petition, the petitioner seeks quashing of the impugned endorsement at Annexure-G dated 11.08.2021 issued by the 3rd respondent and for other reliefs.

2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for respondents and perused the material on record.
3.

In addition to reiterating the various contentions urged in the petition, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that pursuant to issuance of preliminary notification dated 24.04.2007 and final notification on 28.08.2008, the respondents took possession of the subject land from the petitioner on 17.08.2008 despite which respondents did not pass any award in favour of the petitioner.
However subsequently, pursuant to agreement dated 29.12.2010, the petitioner received amounts from the respondents towards compensation.

Thereafter, petitioner submitted a representation dated 30.09.2010 calling upon the respondents to pay additional sum to the petitioner by way of solatium and interest on the market value and since the respondents did not consider the said Basavaraj S/O Shivarayappa Badiger vs State Of Karnataka on 12 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43853541/
2 request, petitioner preferred W.P.No.64215/2012 before this Court.

When the said W.P.No.64215/2012 preferred by the petitioner was pending consideration before this Court,
adjacent land-losers whose lands were also acquired under the very same notifications dated 24.04.2007 and 28.08.2008 approached this Court in a batch/series of writ petitions in the case of Suresh D.Bankapur V/s State of Karnataka and others - W.P.No.64214/2012 and connected matters as detailed hereunder.

sentences.text: 4. It is relevant to state that except W.P.No.64215/2012 preferred by the petitioner herein, all the aforesaid remaining matters arising out of the very same notifications including the case of Suresh D.Bankapur- W.P.No.64214/2012 came up before this Court on 09.07.2012.
By separate identical orders dated 09.07.2012, a learned single Judge of this Court dismissed the petitions preferred by the adjacent land owners.

5. Aggrieved by the aforesaid orders dated 09.07.2012 passed by this Court in Suresh D.Bankapur case supra and other connected matters, the respective land owners-writ petitioners preferred appeals before the Hon'ble Division Bench.

While some of writ appeals preferred by the land owners were dismissed, other writ appeals preferred by other land owners were allowed by the Hon'ble Division Bench thereby awarding additional sums of money in favour of the land owners.
The landloosers and the authorities approached the Hon'ble Apex Court in Civil Appeal Nos.2380-2383/2017 and connected matters.

By final order dated 30.01.2018, the Hon'ble Apex Court disposed off the said appeals directing the respondents- authorities to grant damages at 15%
per annum on the amount of compensation from the date of taking possession till the date of payment.

The said order of the Hon'ble Apex Court reads as under:
"1. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2. Delay condoned and leave granted in all the special leave petitions.
3.

The central issue involved in the appeals is :
whether after entering into an agreement, the appellants are entitled to further amount of solatium and interest.
The High Court has declined solatium and interest in view of the terms of agreement entered into between the parties.

In the agreement it was made clear that the amount offered was total compensation to be received by the appellants and they have also waived their rights to claim higher compensation before the Civil Court.
Thus, they have accepted compensation determined without protest and by way of agreement.

In similar situations, this Court, in Ranveer Singh Vs. State of U.P., reported in (2016) 14 SCC 191; and in the case of State of Gujarat &
Ors. Vs. Daya Shamji Bhai & Ors., reported in (1995) 5 SCC 746,

Hence, appellants are not entitled to solatium and interest.
4. It is also not in dispute that possession had been taken earlier, approximately three years before, whereas agreement had been entered into in the year 2010.

3 of fact, though the appellants cannot be said to be entitled to solatium and interest in view of the agreement that had been entered into, but since the possession had been taken at an earlier point of time, they would be entitled for damages for the interregnum period, i.e., from the date of taking decision till the date when the amount was paid to them under the agreement.

5. This Court, in the case of Revenue Divisional Officer, Kurnool Dist. Vs. M.
Ramakrishna Reddy (D) By LRs., reported in 2011 (11) SCC 648, has laid down that though interest was not payable but damages can be measured and awarded in such cases.

sentences.text: Thus, in the instant cases, we deem it appropriate to exercise our inherent power under Article 142 of the Constitution of India to grant damages @15% per annum on the amount of compensation from the date the possession was taken till the amount was paid.
6. Let the amount of interest be worked out and paid to the appellants within two months from today.
In all the appeals, order passed by the High Court is modified accordingly.
5. With the above modification, the appeals stand disposed of along with all the pending applications.
1. We find no merit in this appeal.
The civil appeal is dismissed.

Pending application,
if any, stands disposed of."

6. Subsequent to the aforesaid matters being disposed off by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Suresh D.Bankapur case supra and connected matters, W.P.No.64215/2012 preferred by the petitioner herein came up for consideration before this Court on 26.11.2019.

After hearing the parties, this Court took note of the order of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Suresh D.Bankapur supra dated 30.01.2018 referred to supra and disposed off the petition directing the respondents to consider the representation of the petitioner herein bearing in mind the judgment of the Apex Court in Suresh D.Bankapur supra.

The order dated 26.11.2019 passed by this Court in W.P.No.64215/2012 preferred by the petitioner herein reads as under:
"In this writ petition, the petitioner has sought for the following relief:
i) Issue a writ of mandamus directing the 3rd respondent to consider the representation at Annexure-D dated 30.09.2011 and make payment of solatium and interest on market value;
i) (a) writ of mandamus directing the respondent No.3 to consider the representation vide Annexure-B1 dated 16.2.2009 Basavaraj S/O Shivarayappa Badiger vs State Of Karnataka on 12 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43853541/
4 ii) Pass such other order as deemed fit in the interest of justice and equity.
2. The case of the petitioner is that he has purchased a plot bearing No.14 in Block/Survey No.639/B measuring 1 gunta 11.25 annas situated at Unkal village, Hubli.
It is the further case of the petitioner that respondent No.1 has initiated acquisition proceedings under the Karnataka Industrial Area Development Act for the purpose of expansion of Hubli Air Port.
Pursuant to that, a notification has been issued under Section 28(6) of the Act and possession has been taken.
The parties have entered into an agreement as per Section 29 of the Act and compensation has been paid from the date of the notification.
The grievance of the petitioner is that the petitioner has given a representation vide annexure-D seeking compensation from the date of taking possession.
In support of his representation Annexure-D, the petitioner has submitted a judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Civil Appeal Nos.2380-2383 of 2017 disposed off on 30.01.2018.
In addition to that the petitioner has given one more representation vide Anexure-B1 dated 16.02.2009 seeking compensation in respect of the building.
Since the same is not considered, the petitioner is before this Court.

3. Learned counsel appearing for respondent Nos.2 to 4 submits that if this Court grants reasonable time, the representations submitted by the petitioner vide Anneuxres-D and B1 will be considered in accordance with law.

4. In view of the submission made by counsel for respondent Nos.2 to 4, this petition is disposed off directing respondent Nos.2 to 4 to consider the representations of the petitioner dated 30.09.2011 and 16.02.2009 vide Annexures- D and B1 in accordance with law taking into consideration the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Suresh D. Bankapur and Ors. Vs. State of Karnataka and Ors. within six months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order."

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Subsequent to the directions issued by this Court referred to supra, the petitioners submitted one more representation dated 27.01.2021 calling upon the respondents to pay additional amounts as directed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in relation to Suresh D.Bankapur and other adjacent land owners.

It is the grievance of the petitioner that despite the aforesaid facts and circumstances and specific orders passed by the Apex Court and directions issued by this Court in the earlier round of litigation in relation to the petitioner herein, the 3rd respondent/SLAO has issued the impugned endorsements rejecting the claim of the petitioner, aggrieved by which the petitioner is before this Court by way of present petition.

8. The respondents have opposed the present petition by filing their statement of objections interalia contending that having regard to the undisputed fact that petitioner entered into an agreement waiving his right for all additional compensation, the question of directing the payment of damages at 15% per annum as directed by the Hon'ble Apex Court does not arise.

It is also pointed out that order passed by the Apex Court in Suresh D.Bankapur case supra was by - 11 - Basavaraj S/O Shivarayappa Badiger vs State Of Karnataka on 12 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43853541/
5 invoking inherent powers exercised under Article 142 of the Constitution of India and consequently,
the question of extending the same benefit to the present petitioner herein does not arise.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is therefore submitted that there is no merit in the petition and same is liable to be dismissed.

9. In my considered opinion, the impugned endorsement at Annexure-G is illegal, arbitrary and the same deserves to be quashed and necessary directions are to be issued to the respondents to pay damages to the petitioner in terms of the judgment of the Apex Court in Suresh D.Bankapur supra for the following reasons.

i) The undisputed material on record indicates that along with the present petitioner,
adjacent land owners had also preferred aforesaid batch of petitions; infact Suresh D.Bankapur who was the lead petitioner/appellant before the Apex Court had preferred W.P.No.64214/2012 whereas present petitioner had preferred W.P.No.64215/2012.
By order dated 09.07.2012, all the petitions preferred by all adjacent land owners including Suresh D.Bankapur were rejected by learned singe Judge of this Court.

However, W.P.No.64215/2012 preferred by - 12 - the petitioner was not disposed off by this Court and the same was pending consideration.
ii) As stated supra, the series of cases/litigations which were initiated by Suresh D.Bankapur and other land-losers excluding the petitioner culminated in the order passed by the Apex Court in Civil Appeal No.2380/2017 dated 30.01.2018.

However as stated supra, since W.P.No.64215/2012 preferred by the petitioner herein was not disposed off with other connected matters all of which disposed off on 09.07.2012, W.P.No.64215/2012 preferred by the petitioner did not reach the Apex Court and was not taken up for consideration by the Apex Court.

iii) It is relevant to state that as can be seen from the order of the Apex Court, the Apex Court has taken note of the fact that the land owners had entered into agreements during the period from 27.10.2010 to 29.12.2010 prior to which possession had already been taken on 17.08.2008 itself on account of which the Apex Court proceeded to direct the respondents to grant damages at 15% per annum on the amount of compensation from the date of - 13 - taking possession till the date of amount was paid on 27.12.2010.

In other words, the Apex Court took note of the fact that the compensation pursuant to the agreement entered into by the respective land owners was paid by the respondent-authorities only subsequently after possession had been taken earlier itself and in order to mitigate the hardship and loss caused to the respective land owners on account of losing possession earlier and compensation being paid subsequently.

Under these circumstances, the Apex Court deemed it just and appropriate to direct the respondents to pay compensation at 15% per annum only for the period from the date of taking of possession till date of amounts were paid in terms of the agreement entered into between the parties.

It is therefore clear Basavaraj S/O Shivarayappa Badiger vs State Of Karnataka on 12 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43853541/
6 that the directions were issued by the Apex Court to pay damages at 15% p.a. to the respective land losers based on possession having been taken earlier and receiving compensation later pursuant to agreements entered by the respective land losers.

entities.text: Basavaraj S/O Shivarayappa Badiger vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Under these circumstances, I am of the considered opinion that in the instant case also, since the petitioner - 14 - had undisputedly lost possession on 17.08.2008 and compensation was received by him only on 29.12.2010, by applying doctrine of parity the petitioner herein who is situated and stands in an exactly similar and identical situation to the other land losers who were before the Apex Court,
petitioner would also be entitled to damages at 15% per annum on the amount of compensation from the date of taking possession i.e. 17.08.2008 till 29.12.2010 when the petitioner received compensation.
iv) A perusal of the earlier order passed by this Court in W.P.No.64215/2012 dated 26.11.2019 will indicate that the said order was passed by this Court subsequent to the order of the Apex Court in Suresh D.Bankapur case supra dated 30.01.2018.
Infact in its order, this Court has specifically directed the respondents to consider the claim of the petitioner bearing in mind the judgment of the Apex Court in Suresh D.Bankapur.

Under these circumstances, the impugned endorsement issued by the 3rd respondent is contrary to the directions issued by this Court in earlier round of litigation and on this ground also, impugned endorsement deserves to be set aside.

Insofar as contention urged by the learned counsel for the respondents that having entered into an agreement, the petitioner is estopped from seeking any additional amount is concerned, as stated earlier, despite noticing the land losers had executed agreement in favour of the respondents, the Apex Court deemed it fair, just and proper to mitigate the hardship and loss caused to the respective land losers by directing payment of damages at 15% per annum from the date of losing possession till date of actual payment and consequently in the light of the judgment of the Apex Court which was rendered in relation to adjacent land losers, the claim of the petitioner which also out of the very same notification deserves to be upheld on the ground of parity and the said contention urged by the learned counsel cannot be accepted.
10.

Insofar as the contention of the learned counsel that the order passed by the Apex Court was rendered by invoking powers under Article 142 is concerned, apart from the fact that the adjacent land losers were before the Apex Court which granted them damages as stated supra, by applying and invoking doctrine of parity and in the light of the directions - 16 - issued by this Court in W.P.No.64215/2012, I am of the considered opinion that since the intention of the Apex Court in granting damages from the date of taking possession till date of payment was in order to mitigate hardship caused to the land losers who were deprived of the land for the said Basavaraj S/O Shivarayappa Badiger vs State Of Karnataka on 12 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43853541/
7 period, is a clear pointer to the fact that the present petitioner who is also situated under identical and similar circumstances would also be entitled to the same benefit given to the adjacent land owners by the Apex Court.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Under these circumstances, even this contention urged by the learned counsel for the respondents cannot be accepted.

In the result, I pass the following:
ORDER i. The petition is allowed.
ii. The impugned endorsement dated 11.08.2021 is hereby set aside.
iii. The concerned respondents are directed to pay damages at 15% per annum as directed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Suresh D.Bankapur V/s State of Karnataka and others, W.P.No.64214/2012 from 18.08.2008 till 29.12.2010 in favour of the petitioner on the amounts of compensation already received by - 17 - the petitioner as expeditiously as possible and within a period of three months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
